title: Unsafe Java Deserialization via ObjectInputStream
platform_conditions: Scala 2.13 / Scala 3 standard library on the JVM; inherits Java serialization semantics of the underlying JVM
security_mechanism: readObject does not parse data -- it executes Java serialization's reconstruction protocol, invoking readObject/defaultReadObject and readResolve on whatever classes the stream names, so any class on the classpath with gadget behavior becomes reachable from the payload alone. Scala code inherits this wholesale: Java serialization is the default wire format for several Scala remote-messaging and remoting stacks unless explicitly switched to a schema format, and polymorphic JSON binding that encodes a class name ('className'/'type' fields) resolves and instantiates attacker-named types the same way.

source_sink_clues.source: Network streams, message-queue payloads, caches, and RPC frames that carry Java-serialized bytes or type-tagged JSON.
source_sink_clues.sink: ObjectInputStream.readObject on attacker-influenced streams; remote-message pipelines left on default Java serialization; polymorphic JSON decoders resolving class names from the payload

tracking_guards: Check the stream is protected by a resolving ObjectInputFilter (JEP 290 serial filter or a validating wrapper) with an explicit class allowlist, an integrity check (HMAC) is verified before readObject, or the wire format is schema-based (protobuf/Jackson with type restriction disabled).
not_candidate_when: The bytes are produced and consumed within one trust boundary with no network exposure, a serial filter allowlists the exact application classes, or a MAC over the payload is verified before deserialization with a non-readable key.
